private_note: My household's number decides it: Cedar 122, Today 108, Alder 106, Birch 90, Hazel 86. Cedar is a real gain for us, but it cuts the lowest fifth to 15, so I doubt it can reach nine votes. Alder costs us only 2 and is the likeliest compromise, so I will signal openness to it. Birch and Hazel cut us by 18-22 thousand, a hit to our mortgage and savings; I would rather the convention fail.
statement: I'm a hospital nurse; my husband is a police officer. Two kids in public school, a mortgage, retirement contributions every month. We're the households that keep this country running, and we're in the fourth fifth. I'll be plain about my interest. Cedar raises our income the most and grows the whole economy by fifteen percent, and I rank it first. But I also see how hard it hits the lowest fifth, and I know it needs nine votes. Hazel and Birch would cut a household like mine by roughly a fifth. That means missed mortgage payments and empty retirement accounts for people who already work nights and weekends. I can't support either, and I'd rather keep today's arrangements than adopt them. Alder is different: a guaranteed floor and basic health coverage at a small cost to households like mine. If Cedar can't carry the room, Alder is where I'm willing to meet you.
